Missing CCSS certification leaves crypto custody controls unvalidated, increasing the risk of undetected security gaps.

reviews.text: Hivemapper is a DePIN mapping project using dashcams, rewarding users in HONEY. Launched in 2022, it competes with Google Maps. In 2025, it sells AI-driven map data. Led by ex-Uber executives.

Secret Network is a L1 blockchain that natively supports private smart contracts (it is based on CosmWasm, a smart contract platform for the Cosmos ecosystem) and it uses Intel SGX (Software Guard Extensions). It was the first of a kind to deliver shielded smart contracts on a public chain. I see it as an Ethereum with all data encrypted by default. Users can even make other tokens private using Secret Bridges. In 2025 it has an active developer community and even a new “Secret AI” layer with on-chain LLMs inside TEEs (TEE refers to a secure area of a processor where data is inaccessible to any other component in the system, increasing security overall).

Secret Network is the first smart contract blockchain to build in privacy by design. I admire this mission it allows developers to write contracts and apps where data stays encrypted, a capability that no other major chain has by default. That could unlock entirely new use cases like private auctions. The trade off is that it’s less decentralized only a few dozen validator nodes. In my mind, it’s a powerful niche tool, but I’m not sure if it will become widely used, given the extra complexity of managing private contracts.

Secret Network is a blockchain that focuses on privacy-first smart contracts. Unlike most public blockchains, Secret allows for “secret contracts” where data is encrypted and kept private by default. This makes it an attractive platform for applications that require privacy, such as in the fields of finance, identity protection, and secure data storage.
